when OpenCode caches only the opencode/ subdirectory (rio-ap, #5); the

Release 0.8.2: OpenCode plugin loads from a git install

The plugin resolves hooks/shared.mjs and skills from the published package
when OpenCode caches only the opencode/ subdirectory (rio-ap, #5); the
install command names the #main ref.

fix(reference): cage open/read/close in preserving_site

A throw while reading the source image left it open as the user's active
sprite, and only app.sprite was restored, never layer or frame.

Reported in #6.
Declare expected reply fields for look, read_pixels, palette and tileset

-      # The Aseprite-backed suite cannot run here — no runner has Aseprite — so
-      # without this the whole Lua half of the project ships on a green pipeline
-      # that never executed a line of it. These are the parts that do not need
-      # the editor: table shape, CIELAB, hex, the autotile mask set.
+      # The Aseprite-backed suite runs in the `lua-handlers` job below. These
+      # are the parts that need no editor at all (table shape, CIELAB, hex, the
+      # autotile mask set), so they stay here where they finish in seconds
+      # instead of waiting on an Aseprite build.
       - name: Run the Aseprite-free Lua tests
         run: lua tests/pure.test.lua
 
+  # Runs the real command handlers against a real Aseprite, headless. No hosted
+  # runner ships Aseprite and its licence forbids redistributing binaries, so
+  # the job builds the scripting-enabled CLI variant (no UI, no Skia) from the
+  # public source and keeps the result in a private Actions cache.
+  lua-handlers:
+    name: Lua handlers (Aseprite CLI)
+    # Pinned rather than `latest`: the cached binary links the runner's system
+    # libraries, so an image bump must not reuse a binary built against the old.
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    env:
+      # The extension targets Aseprite 1.3.x; this is the version it is
+      # developed against. Bump together with the cache key (it embeds the tag).
+      ASEPRITE_TAG: v1.3.17
+      ASEPRITE_HOME: ${{ github.workspace }}/.aseprite-cli
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+      - name: Install build and runtime dependencies
+        run: |
+          sudo apt-get update -qq
+          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+            g++ cmake ninja-build git ca-certificates \
+            libpixman-1-dev libfreetype6-dev libharfbuzz-dev zlib1g-dev \
+            libx11-dev libxcursor-dev libxi-dev libxrandr-dev libgl1-mesa-dev \
+            libfontconfig1-dev
+      - name: Restore the Aseprite CLI build
+        id: aseprite-cache
+        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
+        with:
+          path: ${{ env.ASEPRITE_HOME }}
+          key: aseprite-cli-${{ env.ASEPRITE_TAG }}-ubuntu-24.04-${{ runner.arch }}
+      - name: Build Aseprite CLI
+        if: steps.aseprite-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
+        run: |
+          git clone --recursive --shallow-submodules --depth 1 \
+            --branch "$ASEPRITE_TAG" https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite "$RUNNER_TEMP/aseprite"
+          # LAF_BACKEND=none is upstream's own `cli` variant: scripting and
+          # batch mode without a window system, so no Skia download.
+          cmake -S "$RUNNER_TEMP/aseprite" -B "$RUNNER_TEMP/aseprite/build" -G Ninja \
+            -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
+            -DLAF_BACKEND=none \
+            -DENABLE_SCRIPTING=ON \
+            -DENABLE_TESTS=OFF \
+            -DENABLE_UPDATER=OFF \
+            -DENABLE_CCACHE=OFF
+          cmake --build "$RUNNER_TEMP/aseprite/build" --target aseprite
+          # The binary resolves its `data/` directory next to itself, so the
+          # whole bin/ directory is what gets cached.
+          mkdir -p "$ASEPRITE_HOME"
+          cp -R "$RUNNER_TEMP/aseprite/build/bin/." "$ASEPRITE_HOME/"
+      # Saved right after the build, not in a post step: a post-step save only
+      # runs when the whole job passes, so a red suite would rebuild every run.
+      - name: Save the Aseprite CLI build
+        if: steps.aseprite-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
+        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
+        with:
+          path: ${{ env.ASEPRITE_HOME }}
+          key: aseprite-cli-${{ env.ASEPRITE_TAG }}-ubuntu-24.04-${{ runner.arch }}
+      # Aseprite's Lua has no os.exit, so the suite reports through its last
+      # line rather than the exit code; a crash before that line must fail too.
+      - name: Run the Aseprite-backed Lua suite
+        run: |
+          "$ASEPRITE_HOME/aseprite" -b --script-param root=. --script tests/extension.test.lua 2>&1 | tee extension-test.log
+          grep -qx 'RESULT: PASS' extension-test.log
+

     name: Package contents
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest

@@ -6,6 +6,22 @@ All notable changes to this project are documented here. Format follows
 
 ## [Unreleased]
 
+### Changed
+
+- CI now builds Aseprite 1.3.17's CLI variant from source (cached) and runs
+  the headless Lua handler suite, which previously ran only on a developer's
+  machine; a handler regression now fails the pipeline.
+
+### Fixed
+
+- `reference` no longer leaves the source image open as the active sprite when
+  reading it fails, and now restores the user's active layer and frame too, not
+  only the sprite.
+- `look`, `read_pixels`, `palette` and `tileset` now refuse a reply from an
+  outdated extension that lacks the fields they summarise, with an
+  `install-extension` hint, instead of reporting `undefined` or an empty
+  palette as if the call worked.
+
 ## [0.8.2] — 2026-10-12
 
 ### Fixed

+  -- preserving_site restores sprite, layer and frame on every path, and the
+  -- source is closed even when reading it throws, so a bad file never leaves a
+  -- stranger's tab open in the user's window.
+  local flat, sw, sh
+  preserving_site(function()
+    local source = app.open(path)
+    if not source then fault("aseprite_error", "Could not open '" .. path .. "'.") end
+    local ok, err = pcall(function()
+      flat = Image(source.width, source.height, ColorMode.RGB)
+      flat:drawSprite(source, source.frames[1])
+      sw, sh = source.width, source.height
+    end)
+    pcall(function() source:close() end)
+    if not ok then error(err, 0) end
+  end)

+title: Jelly slime spike slam
+description: A 64×64 jelly slime enemy whose 18-frame attack jumps, slams down and spreads into a puddle, grows goo spikes, then wobbles back into its dome.
+date: 2026-10-18
+author: { name: Nik Fedorov, github: fedorovvvv }
+plugin: 0.8.0
+harness: omp
+models: [claude-opus-5-5]
+tags: [character, monster, slime, animation, 64x64]
+references:
+  source: none
+steps:
+  - text: |-
+      Character - slime
+      Animation: attack type. It jumps up, hits the ground and flattens, after which spikes grow upward out of it. Then it turns back
+    original: |-
+      Персонаж - слайм
+      Анимация: тип атака. Подпрыгивает вверх, ударяется об землю и расплющивается, после чего из него вырастают шипы вверх. Потом превращается обратно
+    interventions:
+      - "Asked to confirm the brief (48×48, Resurrect 64, side view, ~13-frame attack) and whether to generate reference images; answered: «Надо чуть больше сетку сделать. Без референсов продолжаем» (make the grid a bit bigger; continue without references) — canvas became 64×64."
+  - text: Make it more jelly-like, and let it spread out more after the jump
+    original: Надо сделать его более желеобразным и пусть после прыжка он больше растекается
+    interventions: []
+files:
+  - { path: jelly-slime-spike-slam.gif, role: cover, label: "The attack, 4×", step: 2 }
+  - { path: jelly-slime-spike-slam-strip.png, role: filmstrip, label: "All 18 frames, 4×", step: 2 }
+  - { path: jelly-slime-spike-slam.aseprite, role: source, label: Source document, step: 2 }
+validate:
+  - { step: 1, passed: true, score: 20, errors: 0, warnings: 16 }
+  - { step: 2, passed: true, score: 5, errors: 0, warnings: 19 }
